title: Yamikin Ushijima-kun
synopsis: In recent years, Japan has become the shining light of Asia, with its noteworthy achievements in the fields of Science and Technology, Medicine and the like. But while there are a great number of rich and successful Japanese people, there are even more who're engaged in a furious struggle simply to earn their day-to-day living expenses -- all the while battling dangerous and money-consuming addictions such as gambling and alcoholism. What will these people do when they require the cash to feed the never-ending desires that are part and parcel of being human? How miserable and dangerous might their lives become if they fall into traps set by black market money-lenders to ensnare just such weak-willed individuals? Note: Won the 56th Shogakukan Manga Award for general manga in 2011. And the 23rd Japan Media Arts Festival Social Impact Award in 2020.

Wasn't the possessed person executed in the past? Is 'Aridna' still alive? Brinny decides to reclaim the empty space left by the disappearance of her precious people. title: Hyang-Dan Dyeon
synopsis: Job seeker Yu Hyang-Gi, struggling day by day, one day finds herself possessed by Hyang-Dan, the character from the traditional Korean folktale Chunhyangjeon. A supporting character, not even the heroine? How wonderful! Our beautiful young lady Chunhyang, and even a madam who cares for her like her own daughter. Hyang-Dan, who only felt the warmth of family after being possessed by the novel, was enjoying a peaceful life. Until "him" showed up! The world's ultimate villain, Byun Hak-Do, is destined to harass Chunhyang and be executed by the male protagonist, Lee Mong-Ryong. How dare he look down on our Chunhyang! "I don't know who you are, but you're a brat." "I've been waiting." "That's why I'm offering you this. An honor no one else can attain." But why do you keep entangling yourself with me? Why does that man care more about me than Chunhyang? A romantic fantasy about Hyang-Dan and Byeon Hak-Do, a twist on classic novels, Hyangdan's Tale. (Source: Kakaopage, translated)
